newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share prices down on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share prices down on profit taking.

text.p: Nigerian blue chips ended the week lower as investors sold for cash, traders said on Friday.
The all-share index, however, rose slightly to 6524.01 from 6515.57 on Thursday.
"People are selling shares because they need cash," one trader said, adding "Schools have just re-opened and parents have fees to pay."
Nigerian Breweries fell by 37 kobo to 12.28 naira, its biggest drop this month.
Guinness fell on announcement on Friday of a decline in its half year profits. It closed 10 kobo down at 8.70 naira.
Dunlop also ended 10 kobo lower at 11.90 naira as did Afribank at 5.50 naira and Vitafoam at 4.90 naira.
Delta Glass lost the maximum five percent, closing 28 kobo down at 5.51 naira.
Big gains were made by National Oil, Cadbury and Benue Cement. National Oil added 70 to 32.20 naira, Cadbury rose 50 to 26.90 naira and Benue Cement finished 25 up at 6.00 naira.
Other big finishers included Guaranty Trust Bank, up 15 kobo at 13.50 naira, AIICO Insurance was 10 kobo higher to 6.90 naira while Texaco added 25 kobo to 26.00 naira.
